meta.title: Requirements Register
meta.subtitle: Every requirement stated in the project brief, decomposed into atomic, testable items with acceptance criteria, priority, status and an official source where one applies.
meta.brief_source: Project brief issued by the repository owner, 2026-11-14 (session 64164906).

status_legend.implemented: Built, running in CI, and verified against an official source.
status_legend.partial: Built and verified for part of its scope; the remainder is listed on the Flagged for Review page.
status_legend.planned: Specified here; not yet implemented. A suggestion on the Suggestions page proposes the path.
status_legend.blocked: Cannot start until an open question is answered.

priority_legend.P0: Must exist before any decision is made on the platform.
priority_legend.P1: Required before the platform produces a publishable line or a leaderboard result.
priority_legend.P2: Improves quality or cost; can follow P0/P1.

requirements.requirement: Collect, organize and analyse a full list of requirements rather than working from an implicit brief.
requirements.rationale: Without a written register, scope, status and acceptance criteria cannot be audited or handed over.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Every requirement in the brief appears as a numbered row with rationale, acceptance criteria, priority, status and source.
requirements.verification: This register is the artefact; row-by-row cross-check against the brief is recorded in docs/requirements-crosswalk.md.

requirements.requirement: Make suggestions to improve the site and to improve decision making, and give them their own section so a reviewer can compare options and choose a path before anything is implemented.
requirements.rationale: The owner wants to review and select, not to have changes applied unilaterally.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: A Suggestions page lists each suggestion with the problem it addresses, at least two alternative paths, expected impact, cost, risk, dependencies, a recommended path and a status that stays 'proposed' until a human chooses.
requirements.verification: suggestions.html renders every suggestion with a decision-path comparison and an explicit 'awaiting review' state.

requirements.requirement: Publish a clear list of the questions, the information and the answers that must be settled before any decision can reasonably be made on the information currently held and not held.
requirements.rationale: Most bad decisions here come from acting on partial information; the gap must be explicit.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: A Questions page lists every open question with why it matters, what is already known (with an official source), what is missing, how to obtain it, whether it blocks a decision, and an owner.
requirements.verification: questions.html renders the full register with known/unknown columns and source links.

requirements.requirement: Include suggestions for discovering information that is currently missing.
requirements.rationale: An open question with no route to an answer is dead weight.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Every question row carries a concrete 'how to obtain' step naming the official source or the person who can answer.
requirements.verification: questions.html 'How to obtain' column is populated for all blocking and non-blocking questions.

requirements.requirement: Produce an executive summary of the important details.
requirements.rationale: The owner needs a single readable artefact before drilling into detail.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: An Executive Summary page states purpose, current state, headline findings, the decisions that are ready, the decisions that are blocked, and the top recommended next actions.
requirements.verification: executive-summary.html is linked from the landing page and from every subpage navigation.

requirements.requirement: Operate with no manual input from the owner during construction.
requirements.rationale: Delivery must be autonomous and reproducible.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The fetch, dataset, signal, site and validation steps all run unattended in CI on a schedule; the owner is never asked to supply data.
requirements.verification: .github/workflows/data-pipeline.yml runs on schedule and on push with no manual step.

requirements.requirement: Coordinate with any other agent sessions working on the repository at the same time, using a shared task board.
requirements.rationale: Parallel sessions otherwise duplicate work or overwrite each other.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: COORDINATION.md lists every task with status, owning session, branch and file scope; claims are committed and pushed before work starts.
requirements.verification: COORDINATION.md present at repository root with the task board, change-request table and log.

requirements.requirement: Ship the work as a pull request to main and publish it, without waiting for the owner's review.
requirements.rationale: The owner asked for end-to-end delivery; flagged items are surfaced on the site instead of blocking the merge.
requirements.verification: Pull request and merge are recorded in COORDINATION.md with the PR link and the merge result.

requirements.requirement: Review the repository line by line, verify each item against official trusted sources, provide links for manual review, and flag any irregularities.
requirements.rationale: The owner needs an auditable trail rather than assertions.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: A source manifest lists every official URL used with its SHA-256 and fetch timestamp; an irregularities page lists anything anomalous.
requirements.verification: data/datasets/fetch_manifest.json and the site's Sources page expose the URL and hash for every dataset.

requirements.requirement: Every published table row must carry a source link to an official site.
requirements.rationale: Unsourced rows are not usable for a decision.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: scripts/validate_site.py fails the build if any dataset row lacks source_url, and every rendered table exposes the link.
requirements.verification: The validator is executed in CI; its output is published on the site's Validation page.

requirements.requirement: If a value cannot be confirmed from an official source, leave it blank and flag it as unverified. Never infer or fill in values.
requirements.rationale: Fabricated values are the single most damaging failure mode for a decision-support system.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Empty cells are rendered as an explicit 'unverified' marker, never as a zero, dash, or best guess; a Flagged for Review page lists every such cell.
requirements.verification: The validator counts blank cells per dataset and the Flagged for Review page reproduces them with their source link.

requirements.requirement: Ingest official data programmatically and reproducibly rather than by hand.
requirements.rationale: Hand-transcribed numbers are unauditable and drift.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: scripts/fetch_official.py pulls only official domains, caches raw payloads, and records status, byte count, SHA-256 and UTC timestamp for each.
requirements.verification: data/datasets/fetch_manifest.json contains one record per source with sha256 and fetched_at.

requirements.requirement: Work only from official NFL and official club sources.
requirements.rationale: Third-party aggregators introduce licensing and accuracy risk.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The source registry contains only nfl.com, operations.nfl.com and official club domains.
requirements.verification: scripts/lib/official.py is the single registry; no other host appears in it.

requirements.requirement: Keep the published data fresh without owner intervention.
requirements.rationale: The injury report changes four times a week during the season.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: A scheduled workflow re-fetches, rebuilds and republishes on a fixed cadence, and every table shows the age of the underlying fetch.
requirements.verification: The data-pipeline workflow runs on schedule; each table carries a 'data as of' timestamp.

requirements.requirement: Originate our own NFL lines rather than consuming someone else's.
requirements.rationale: The owner wants independent signal generation, not redistribution of a commercial book's numbers.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: A published line model produces spread and total lines from official data, with a documented methodology and a stated margin; no commercial line is ingested.
requirements.verification: scripts/compute_signals.py emits data/datasets/our_lines.json; the Sources page states that no third-party line feeds are used.

requirements.requirement: Research and develop strategies for generating useful signals.
requirements.rationale: A signal is only useful if it survives validation and produces a measurable edge.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Every strategy has a stated hypothesis, an explicit signal definition computed from official data, a validation plan and a current status.
requirements.verification: strategies.html lists each strategy with hypothesis, signal, inputs and status.

requirements.requirement: Treat the work as a leaderboard competition that rewards top performing strategies.
requirements.rationale: A competitive frame forces every strategy to be measurable and comparable.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: A leaderboard specification defines entrants, scoring, gates, tie-breaks and a reward structure, and a live standings table is published.
requirements.verification: leaderboard.html publishes the scoring specification and the standings table generated from the backtest harness.

requirements.requirement: Cover single bets, parlays and player-prop combinations.
requirements.rationale: The three classes behave differently under correlation and variance.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The strategy register contains entries in each of the three classes and the leaderboard scores them separately.
requirements.verification: strategies.html groups entries by class and each class has at least one entry that reached the validation harness.

requirements.requirement: Every strategy must pass validation gates before it can be deployed or scored.
requirements.rationale: Without gates, the leaderboard rewards luck.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Ten gates (G1-G10) are defined, machine-evaluated from the backtest output, and a strategy that fails any gate is marked ineligible and excluded from rewards.
requirements.verification: The Gates table on strategies.html shows each gate, its threshold and the measured value for every strategy.

requirements.requirement: Determine correlation values between signals and between strategies.
requirements.rationale: Correlated bets multiplied in a parlay create false confidence and fake edge.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: A correlation matrix is computed from official data and published with the method, sample and window stated.
requirements.verification: Correlations are computed by scripts/compute_signals.py and rendered on strategies.html with n and window.

requirements.requirement: Remove luck from the equation and build strategies that are selectively skill-based.
requirements.rationale: A positive record can be pure variance; the platform must separate skill from luck explicitly.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: A published skill-share metric decomposes observed outcome variance into model-implied variance and residual variance, and a strategy is only eligible when the skill share and its confidence interval clear a stated threshold.
requirements.verification: The luck/skill table on strategies.html shows skill share, residual share and the bootstrap interval for each strategy.

requirements.requirement: Selectively pursue strategies that are skill-based rather than betting broadly.
requirements.rationale: Selective edge is the objective; volume is not.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The platform ranks strategies and surfaces only gate-passing entries; non-passing strategies remain visible for audit but carry no reward eligibility.
requirements.verification: leaderboard.html separates 'eligible' from 'ineligible' rows and explains the exclusion reason.

requirements.requirement: Track injuries continuously from official sources.
requirements.rationale: Availability is the largest single driver of NFL prices and of any honest edge.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The official weekly injury report is ingested, parsed and published per player with practice status, game status, injury designation and a source link.
requirements.verification: injuries.html publishes every parsed row; the count is reconciled against the official page.

requirements.requirement: Know deficiencies in defences, including when second, third or fourth string backups are replacing starters because of the lineup.
requirements.rationale: A defence missing its edge rusher is a different bet than one missing its third wideout.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: For each team the platform tracks the depth string of the replacement for each absent starter, and publishes it with the official source for the depth ordering.
requirements.verification: depth.html publishes the depth string for every official absence that can be resolved from an official depth chart. Where no official depth chart exists for the club, the cell is left blank and listed on the Flagged for Review page.

requirements.requirement: Apply the same treatment to offences using starters or backups.
requirements.rationale: Offensive depth is the mirror of defensive depth and moves offensive lines and totals.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Offensive absences are tracked with the same string-depth resolution and the same source requirement.
requirements.verification: depth.html covers both units and flags clubs whose official depth chart could not be retrieved.

requirements.requirement: Distinguish a player who is absent from the report from a player who is healthy.
requirements.rationale: Silence in an injury report is not a clearance.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Rows carry an explicit reported/not-reported flag and the site's methodology states that absence from the report is not evidence of availability.
requirements.verification: Methodology page states the rule and the data pages render the reported flag.

requirements.requirement: Record the timestamp of every injury snapshot so historical analysis uses the report that was actually available at decision time.
requirements.rationale: Back-testing with today's knowledge of an injury is look-ahead bias.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Each snapshot stores the official report's week, game date and the fetch timestamp.
requirements.verification: injuries.json records week, game_date and the manifest records fetched_at and sha256.

requirements.requirement: Create a live GitHub Pages site for the repository.
requirements.rationale: The deliverable has to be reachable and reviewable by the owner.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The site builds in CI and is served from the repository's GitHub Pages URL with a successful deployment.
requirements.verification: GitHub Pages deployment status is checked and the PR/merge record in COORDINATION.md links the live URL.

requirements.requirement: Provide a clean landing page and subpages organised by category.
requirements.rationale: Decision material is only usable if it is navigable.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: A landing dashboard links to every subpage; subpages are grouped under Requirements, Decision Support, Strategy & Competition, Data, and Governance.
requirements.verification: index.html contains the full navigation and the validator checks every navigation link resolves.

requirements.requirement: Keep the UI clean, user friendly, simple and easy to use, like a simple dashboard.
requirements.rationale: A dense research site that nobody reads helps nobody.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: One shared stylesheet, a persistent top navigation, summary cards before tables, and tables that are sortable and filterable by simple client-side JavaScript.
requirements.verification: Site uses a single assets/style.css; every table has a filter box; no page requires horizontal scrolling of the body.

requirements.requirement: Present all entries and findings in a simple, readable table format, including analysis and findings.
requirements.rationale: Tables are the reviewable unit of this project.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Every dataset and every register is rendered as a table with a header row and a source column.
requirements.verification: scripts/validate_site.py asserts that each data page contains at least one table with a Source column.

requirements.requirement: Publish a clearly labelled Flagged for Review page for unverified values, irregularities and anything needing a human decision.
requirements.rationale: Flagged items must be visible without blocking delivery.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: flagged.html lists every flagged item with its reason, the source link that was checked, and what would resolve it.
requirements.verification: The flag register is generated from the same dataset metadata that renders the tables, so no row can be flagged without appearing.

requirements.requirement: Confirm the site builds with no broken links before publishing.
requirements.rationale: A broken link on a decision page is a silent data-quality failure.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: A validator resolves every internal link and every local asset reference, and fails the build when one is broken.
requirements.verification: scripts/validate_site.py runs in CI and its report is published on the Validation page.

requirements.requirement: Verify line by line, with no hallucinations.
requirements.rationale: Trust is the product.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Every published dataset row traces to an official URL; a per-dataset row count is published so a reviewer can reconcile against the official page.
requirements.verification: datasets manifest.json publishes the row count and source for each dataset.

requirements.requirement: Flag any irregularities for review.
requirements.rationale: Silent anomalies become false confidence.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: An irregularity log records every anomaly found during the repo review and every anomaly detected by the validator.
requirements.verification: docs/irregularities.md is rendered on the Flagged for Review page.

requirements.requirement: Keep an audit trail from published number back to the exact official payload it came from.
requirements.rationale: Reproducibility is the only defence against a subtle parsing error.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Each dataset records the SHA-256 of its source payload and the UTC fetch time.
requirements.verification: fetch_manifest.json stores sha256 and fetched_at per source; the Sources page displays them.

requirements.requirement: Final integration must re-verify the combined data line by line and confirm the build before publishing.
requirements.rationale: Merged branches can silently reintroduce stale or duplicated data.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The integration session re-runs the validator over the merged tree, confirms zero broken links, then opens and merges the pull request and records the deployment status.
requirements.verification: The merge record in COORDINATION.md lists the validator output and the GitHub Pages deployment result.
